documents.title: Probiotics and diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania: secondary analysis of a randomised clinical trial.
documents.abstract: Diarrhoea causes annually more than 444 000 deaths in children globally, the majority in infants in low-income countries. The gut microbiota is a key determinant in resilience against enteric infections. We evaluated the effects of Bifidobacterium-based probiotic supplementation on diarrhoea morbidity among infants in Tanzania and explored associations between the gut microbiota composition at 6 weeks of age and later diarrhoeal risk.

documents.title: Assembly of minimally fragmented metagenomic pangenome graphs.
documents.abstract: Pangenome variation graphs are a powerful tool for representing genetic diversity within and across populations. For comparative and evolutionary genomic analyses leveraging these graph-based structures, it is important that graph topology reflects the underlying phylogenetic and genetic similarities of the genomes embedded within the graph. However, in metagenomic settings these approaches often produce highly fragmented multi-component graphs, hindering comparisons of genomes embedded across different components. documents.title: Senimuribacter muris sp. nov., a butyrate-producing bacterium isolated from mouse feces, and reclassification of members of the family Eubacteriaceae into the family Anaerovoracaceae.
documents.abstract: Two strictly anaerobic, Gram-stain-positive, non-motile, and rod-shaped bacterial strains, designated rT4E-8T and mB4P-1, were isolated from the feces of specific-pathogen-free Mus musculus (C57BL/6J). Both strains were catalase- and oxidase-negative and produced butyrate as a major fermentation product, with optimal growth at 37 °C and pH 7. The two strains shared 100% pairwise 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity and showed high similarity to Senimuribacter intestinalis DSM 106208T (95.1-95.3%). documents.title: Shifts in the Maternal Gut Microbiome Across Pregnancy are Associated with Energetic Status in Phayre's Leaf Monkeys.
documents.abstract: During pregnancy, mothers experience physiological changes that support fetal development, including shifts in energy utilization and increasing insulin resistance during late gestation. While these changes benefit the fetus, they can also impose energetic costs that affect the mother's physical condition and metabolic phenotype. Previous studies suggest that the gut microbiome, a key regulator of female metabolism and energy harvest, may play a critical role in mediating these physiological challenges.

documents.title: Disrupted microbial queuosine biosynthesis contributes to dysbiosis in human inflammatory bowel disease.
documents.abstract: As a microbiome/diet-derived vitamin, queuine (q) is a micronutrient that eukaryotes acquire from microbiota or diet. Vitamin q, the free base form of queuosine (Q), is used for Q-modification of transfer RNA (tRNA). Although tRNA-Q-modification in regulating eukaryotic cell physiology is recognized, the relationship between Q-tRNA-modification and the human microbiome in health and inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) remains unknown. documents.title: Scellmate enables contamination aware curation and host mobilome linkage analysis of large SAG datasets.
documents.abstract: Single-cell genomics enables cell-resolved insights into in-situ microbial communities, yet single amplified genomes (SAGs) are often fragmented, taxonomically ambiguous, and prone to contamination, limiting their biological interpretation. Here, we present Scellmate, a scalable, semi-supervised framework that integrates whole-SAG curation, species-level taxonomic anchoring and SAG-mobilome linkage analysis for large-scale SAG datasets. Following benchmarking of its SAG curation and SAG-eMGE linkage modules using in silico and four-strain mock SAG datasets, respectively, Scellmate was applied

documents.title: Draft genome sequences of Desulfobulbus oralis strains reconstructed from archeological dental calculus of ancient Pacific Islanders.
documents.abstract: We present draft metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) of Desulfobulbus oralis strains reconstructed from ancient Pacific Islander dental calculus. MAGs were reconstructed via reference-guided read recruitment, de novo assembly, and metagenomic binning, displaying average nucleotide identities ≥96.4% to the D. oralis ATCC HOT041 reference genome, with completeness ≥50% and contamination ≤2.38%.

documents.title: PEONY: a global reference database of DNA viral (vOTU) sequences from viral size-fractionated metagenomes (viromes).
documents.abstract: We present an update to the Phages and Integrated Genomes Encapsidated or Not reference database of DNA viral sequences (viral operational taxonomic units [vOTUs], mostly dsDNA bacteriophages) from global ecosystems. To reflect the inclusion of only virus size-fractionated metagenome- (virome-)derived vOTUs, we reintroduce the database as Phages Encapsidated ONlY.

documents.title: Temperature effects on life history strategies for rapid growth potential of leaf epiphytic bacteria.
documents.abstract: Phyllosphere bacteria, occupying both epiphytic and endophytic habitats, constitute a critical plant-atmosphere interface. However, their community assembly and life-history strategies (LHSs) in response to temperature increase remain poorly understood. Here, we compared leaf phyllosphere bacterial communities with those in other plant compartments across four representative plant species from an alpine meadow on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. documents.title: Children at risk of vitamin A deficiency exhibit taxonomic dysbiosis and functional remodeling of the gut microbiome: a matched case-control study.
documents.abstract: Vitamin A deficiency is one of the most prevalent micronutrient deficiencies worldwide. This condition increases susceptibility to infections and due to its role in intestinal barrier integrity, it has been suggested that it could predispose to gut dysbiosis.

documents.title: Sex influences the mosquito virome in a host-specific way.
documents.abstract: Mosquitoes harbor diverse eukaryotic viruses. These viral communities, or viromes, probably influence mosquito physiology, including pathogen transmission. However, the factors shaping the virome remain largely unstudied, limiting our understanding of its role in mosquito biology. Here, we assess the influence of sex on the eukaryotic virome of mosquitoes. Ecological differences between males and females, such as female-specific blood feeding, may lead to differential viral exposure and virome structure. documents.title: Diversity and evolution of the ribovirian class Stelpaviricetes.
documents.abstract: Metatranscriptome mining has dramatically expanded the known diversity of ribovirians at all taxonomic levels. We explored the class Stelpaviricetes in the phylum Pisuviricota that currently includes three orders and six recognized virus families: order Stellavirales with family Astroviridae infecting vertebrates; Patatavirales with families Potyviridae, the largest known family of plant ribovirians, and Potyliviridae; and Hypofuvirales consisting of three families of viruses associated largely with phytopathogenic fungi. Using an order-specific collection of Hidden Markov Model profiles for t

documents.title: Monitoring single-cell metabolic phenotyping changes of Daqu microbiota during fermentation by Raman spectroscopy.
documents.abstract: Monitoring microbial community dynamics during natural food fermentation is essential for stabilizing fermentation processes and improving product flavor profiles. This study employed single-cell Raman spectroscopy to monitor the metabolic change of Daqu microbiota during fermentation. First, we developed an operational phenotypic unit (OPU)-based clustering method to process Raman spectral data of a nine-member microbial community. The clustering was validated by sorting out representative single cells from different OPUs and performing 16S/ITS region sequencing. Second, single-cell Raman spe

documents.title: Scaffold-level validation is needed for phage-host inference from metagenome-assembled genomes.
documents.abstract: Accurate phage-host prediction underpins ecological interpretation and experimental validation of uncultivated phages, yet most current approaches rely heavily on metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). This reliance implicitly assumes that MAG-level quality metrics, such as completeness and contamination, ensure scaffold-level correctness. Here, we demonstrate that this assumption can be violated under particular challenging conditions. documents.title: Shotgun metagenomic characterization of human adenovirus F40 and a non-cpe Clostridium perfringens strain in pediatric prolonged diarrhea: a genome-resolved case study.
documents.abstract: Viral and bacterial pathogens may be concurrently detected in pediatric gastroenteritis, yet such findings are often missed by routine diagnostic methods. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing enables comprehensive detection and genomic characterization of microorganisms present in clinical specimens, including pathogens that may not be recovered by conventional testing.

documents.title: Genome-resolved taxonomy, global distribution, and EPS potential of Zoogloea, the canonical floc-former in wastewater treatment systems.
documents.abstract: The bacterial genus Zoogloea is the fourth most abundant genus in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) globally, where it plays key roles in floc formation and nutrient removal but can also contribute to viscous bulking when highly abundant. The taxonomic assignment of Zoogloea has historically been inconsistent, as several taxa were classified based on phenotypic characteristics and later reassigned to other families or orders. This has obscured both the identity and distribution of Zoogloea and hindered interpretation of its floc-forming mechanisms, which have been attributed to polysaccharid

documents.title: Global Carriage of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes and Virulence Factors Among Physicians in Cirrhosis Care.
documents.abstract: Cirrhosis patients are at high risk for drug-resistant infections, which may be transmitted between patients and healthcare providers. In this study, we used shotgun metagenomics to characterize the fecal microbiome of physicians in cirrhosis care (n = 55) across 9 countries. Our results indicate physicians from low- or middle-income countries carry greater antimicrobial resistance gene (ARG) diversity corresponding to increased taxonomic richness. Physicians carried a low prevalence of clinically relevant ARGs or virulence factors (VFs), regardless of country of practice or patient exposure.

documents.title: Importance of rumen ciliated protozoa and current research techniques for their analysis.
documents.abstract: Rumen protozoa are an integral component of the ruminant foregut microbiome, with a profound influence on feed digestion, microbial ecosystem dynamics and enteric methane emissions. Although they represent only a small proportion of species richness, protozoa contribute significantly to microbial biomass and functions in fibre degradation, volatile fatty acid production, microbial protein turnover, pH modulation and hydrogen-mediated methanogenesis. In addition to highlighting their importance to rumen function, this review summarizes classical and contemporary methodologies for enumerating, i

documents.title: Infective endocarditis due to a novel Gemella species revealed by metagenomic sequencing.
documents.abstract: Gemella species are rare causes of infective endocarditis, and accurate species identification can be challenging with routine diagnostic methods. We report infective endocarditis caused by a novel Gemella species, highlighting the diagnostic value of sequencing-based approaches for bacteria not registered in public databases and the risk of misclassification when novel species are not represented in reference databases.

documents.title: Benchmarking nanopore-based strategies for antimicrobial resistance prediction.
documents.abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) presents a pressing need to ensure that the right antimicrobials are used to target the right microbes at the right time. Ideally, the appropriate antimicrobial is selected after patient samples have been cultured and assessed with antimicrobial sensitivity testing (AST). However, the time needed for culture-based diagnosis leads to immediate empirical treatment, often with broad-spectrum and/or high-tier antimicrobials. Direct nanopore metagenomic whole-genome sequencing to identify pathogens and predict their AMR is a rapid and patient-side alternative. A limit

documents.title: Seasonal and Environmental Influences on Microbial Community Dynamics in the Dunk River Watershed, Prince Edward Island, Canada.
documents.abstract: Riverine ecosystems are crucial biogeochemical hubs, with their microbial communities playing a key role in nutrient cycling and overall ecosystem health. This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize the seasonal and environmental drivers of taxonomic and functional microbial community structure (read depth between 1.91 and 30.44 bp) in four tributaries of the Dunk River watershed in Prince Edward Island (PEI), a landscape shaped by intensive agriculture and groundwater-dominated streamflow, where the seasonal and land-use impacts on the river's microbiome remain understudied

documents.title: Strong agreement in absolute marine prokaryote abundance from epifluorescence microscopy and internal-standard-corrected metagenomics.
documents.abstract: Quantifying microbial cell abundance in natural environments with taxonomic resolution remains a central challenge in microbial ecology. While epifluorescence microscopy reliably enumerates free-living cells, it lacks taxonomic specificity and is less suitable for quantifying cells in sediments, soils, and on surfaces. Furthermore, most omics approaches profile microbial communities, but they typically provide only relative abundances. Recent advances in quantitative metagenomics using single-copy marker genes and genomic internal standards enable taxon-specific abundance estimates in absolute

documents.title: Gut‒liver‒brain axis signature of cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment is consistent across multi-national cohorts.
documents.abstract: Cognitive impairment in cirrhosis is associated with an altered gut‒liver‒brain axis, but geographic variations in diet and clinical practices may limit generalizability. We investigated consistency of microbial signatures for cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment across four countries. We enrolled outpatients with cirrhosis from USA, Denmark, Lithuania, and Mexico who underwent Psychometric Hepatic Encephalopathy Score (PHES) testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy (CHE), and stool shotgun metagenomic sequencing. Taxonomic and functional associations with PHES were evaluated after adjustme

documents.title: Deciphering the gut-lung axis in non-small cell lung cancer: from immune microenvironment crosstalk to clinical translation.
documents.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 axis have established a new standard of care for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, clinical efficacy is frequently limited by primary resistance, acquired (secondary) resistance, and immune-related adverse events. The heterogeneity of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) is a critical determinant of therapeutic response, a state effectively regulated by the gut microbiota via the gut-lung axis. This review systematically examines the mechanistic crosstalk between intestinal commensals and the pulmonary TIME. We first d

documents.title: The interaction mechanisms between sarcopenia and gut microbiota based on the gut-muscle axis.
documents.abstract: Advances in high-throughput sequencing and metagenomics have improved our understanding of the gut microbiota and its associations with disease development and treatment response. The relationship between the gut microbiota and sarcopenia has attracted increasing attention in recent years. In this narrative review, we searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CNKI, Wanfang Data, and VIP through April 2,026 and synthesized 29 human studies included in the narrative analysis together with relevant preclinical evidence. We summarize reported alterations in microbial diversity, taxonomic compositio

documents.title: Metagenomic characterization of gut microbiota in patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction.
documents.abstract: Patients with Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBI) experience recurrent gastrointestinal symptoms without identifiable organic abnormalities. While earlier studies focused on neural and hormonal regulation, recent evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolism may play key roles in DGBI.

documents.title: Metagenomic analysis of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes detects Ralstonia phage sequences in Kenyan agricultural soils.
documents.abstract: Bacterial wilt caused by Ralstonia solanacearum species complex is a major constraint in tomato production in Kenya, resulting in yield losses of up to 100% in heavily infested fields. This study used high-throughput shotgun metagenomic sequencing approach to characterize the rhizosphere microbiomes of tomato plants in three of the major production areas in Kenya (Kirinyaga, Kiambu, and Laikipia counties) focusing on detecting Ralstonia phage sequences. Soil samples were collected from the rhizosphere of bacterial wilt-infected tomato plants, and microbial DNA was extracted using a modified ph

documents.title: A systematic review of the effects of diet on the gut microbiota in individuals at elevated risk for colorectal cancer.
documents.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) poses a major public health concern, with emerging evidence highlighting the critical role of the gut microbiota in CRC progression. Considering that diet is a major modifiable factor influencing CRC risk, partly through its interaction with the gut microbiome, this systematic review evaluated the effects of dietary intervention RCTs, including supplements, functional foods, whole foods, and dietary patterns, on the gut microbiome in elevated-risk individuals.

documents.title: Co-occurrence and genetic contexts of NDM-1, KPC-2, IMP-1, and AFM-1 carbapenemase genes in a critically ill patient.
documents.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant organisms are increasingly reported in clinical settings, yet the simultaneous detection of multiple carbapenemase genes within a single specimen remains rare.
